notes:
Lead source: self-serve signup (signup form + quickstart). Team: 2 devs + 1 founder (ex-engineering at mid-saas).

Summary: experimenting with Redwood Hosted API for an in-product code assistant + embeddings-based search. Low volume prototype, high sensitivity to per-token cost. Want predictable latency for short prompts (<200ms ideal for interactive code completions). Currently using small test dataset (~12k tokens) for relevance tuning.

Activity timeline:
- 2026-03-01: signed up via self-serve, created API key, started quickstart repo.
- 2026-03-03: emailed support asking about token pricing tiers and burst limits (thread gmail_thread_17f8b2).
- 2026-03-05: ran initial embedding tests (good quality, costs higher than expected).
- 2026-03-07: slack-style call w/ community QA (no AE). asked about model fallback and rate-limit behavior under congestion.
- 2026-03-09: requested short PR doc: "pricing + minimal config to hit 150ms median latency" (added to drive/pricing-faq-v2.pdf).

Notes from founder (paraphrased): "We want a tiny footprint POC that stays cheap while we validate product-market fit. If latency and cost look good, we'll convert to monthly reserved capacity in 6-12mo."

Technical constraints/requirements (developer notes):
- workload: mix of code completions (short seq) and embedding lookups (vector DB + caching).
- target latency: median <200ms, p95 <500ms for completions.
- throughput: initial 1-5 QPS, bursty during dev demos.
- model preference: open models first; willingness to test Redwood-verified variants.
- routing/fallback: wants automatic fallback to smaller model if rate-limited, but concerned about quality drop.
- security: no sensitive customer PII in test data; wants exportable request logs for debugging and short-term retention.

Open questions / asks for Redwood:
- Can we get a small trial credit top-up for this POC? (stated priority)
- Short doc: recommended batching/cache settings for low-latency code completions.
- Clarify per-minute burst limit and what triggers 429s.

Next actions (recommended):
- Sales ops to evaluate small credit boost (one-off).
- Send tailored one-pager: cost calc + suggested runtime config (batch size, cache TTL).
- Quick dev note on model fallback semantics and sample config for canary fallback to small model.
